$comment: The project's open-items index. Build DNA §8 states the rule this file implements: an ADR that opens or closes an open item records it here. Written once by tools/sync.sh and owned by this project thereafter — sync.sh will not overwrite it, the way it will not overwrite CLAUDE.md.
$authority: This file owns an item's STATE. The prose entry — wherever the ADR put it — owns the argument, and keeps its number and its entry when it closes. Where the two disagree about status, one of them is wrong; that is a defect to fix, not a precedence rule to apply.
$not_gate_input: No gate check reads this file. Keeping it current is a discipline, not a control. See Build DNA open item 6.
standard_version: REPLACE — the Causeway version in .causeway-lock when this register was last reviewed
$registers: A register is any document in this project that carries a numbered list of open items. Most projects have one; some have one per governed document. A numbered list the index does not name is a register nothing counts, which is the state this file exists to end. Delete the example and add your own.
$numbering: number is null only for an item closed by renumbering before this register made its numbers stable. Do not use null for a new item — give it the next number and never reuse one. Renumbering on close is how a pointer comes to reference a different item than the one it closed.

$item_shape.number: the number in the prose list, or null (see $numbering)
$item_shape.title: a short label. The argument stays in the prose entry; nothing checks this string, so rewording it is free
$item_shape.status: open | closed. There is no half-closed: an item is open until every half of it is closed
$item_shape.opened_by: ADR number as a quoted string, e.g. "0007", or null where the record does not state it
$item_shape.opened_in: the version of the register's document, or null
$item_shape.closed_by: ADR number, or null. An item closed by nothing lapsed rather than closed
$item_shape.closed_in: the version it closed in, or null
$item_shape.$note: optional. Anything a reader of this file needs that the prose entry does not carry

items.title: REPLACE — delete this example once the register has a real item

$counts: Derived from items. Every count stated anywhere in the project comes from here. Recompute it in the commit that changes items — a count nobody recomputes is the failure this index was built for.
$relations: An item may name its relationship to another item, or to the document that answered it. Build DNA §8 defines the five types and what each promises; the standard's own decisions/open-items.json is the worked example. They matter as soon as this project has more than one register, and the failures they catch — half a closed duplicate, a question settled elsewhere, a finding filed against the wrong document — are invisible to a count.

relation_types.duplicate_of: item id. Mutual; both halves must carry the same status.
relation_types.superseded_by: item id. When the target closes, this item must close.
relation_types.upstream_of: list of item ids in other registers. When one closes, re-read this item.
relation_types.answered_by: {document, section, summary}. The document must exist and still carry that heading.
relation_types.blocked_on: list of keys from `blockers` below. Every key must be declared.

$blockers: Name what an item is actually waiting on. Delete the example and use your own; a key no item cites fails the build, and so does an item citing a key nothing declares.

blockers.REPLACE-a-real-blocker: What this blocker is, and what would clear it.
